newsitem.title: USA: Calif. water park opens after deadly slide accident.
newsitem.headline: Calif. water park opens after deadly slide accident.

text.p: A California amusement park reopened Saturday nearly two weeks after a water slide accident killed one teen-ager and injured 32 others.
Waterworld USA in Concord, California, about 30 miles northeast of San Francisco, was closed after part of a 40-foot-tall winding slide collapsed on June 2.
Teen-agers on the slide plummeted to the ground. One teen-age girl died and many others broke bones in the fall.
Concord Mayor Bill McManigal said experts brought in to inspect the park after the accident concluded it was safe.
Inspectors believe the water slide gave way because the teen-agers gathered at the top in a large group, putting too much weight on the structure.
The teens were from a high school in Napa, California. They were at Waterworld, owned by Premier Parks Inc., to celebrate their graduation.
